correctness.rationale: The original graph has 36 perfect matchings and 5,407 augmented faces. A completely tested 2,702-pair acyclic Morse matching leaves two critical 2-cells and one critical 3-cell (empty face paired); the full 24,812-incidence Hasse digraph is acyclic. Independently 2,628 certified elementary collapses yield a core with 25 tetrahedra. A displayed nonzero signed integral 25-term top cycle has exact zero boundary; binary rank 24 of the 62-by-25 third boundary proves rank exactly 24 over Q. Therefore rational H3 has rank one and forces the integral single Morse 3-cell attaching column to vanish. Hurewicz for the two-skeleton S2 wedge S2 gives an actual null-homotopic 3-attachment. Integral homotopy type is S2 wedge S2 wedge S3; no unproved infinite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant 2024 primary paper proves the two-row case and explicitly leaves the general rectangular grid wedge question open (Conjecture 6.1). The present four-row, four-column graph fails that domain restriction. The closest indexed four-by-four result is for the ordinary matching complex, whose facets include maximal nonperfect matchings, and is not an implication for the perfect-matching subcomplex. Honeycomb graph results and later circular/Möbius ladder results use different underlying graphs. Several aliases and stronger-covering possibilities were searched; no exact covering claim was found. Index limitations and the inaccessible full text of a later related paper remain residual risks.
residual_risks: Search of a semantic index and selected primary articles cannot exclude obscure, unpublished, untranslated or unindexed equivalent computations.
The 2026 circular/Möbius-ladder paper was only available at abstract level, not compared page by page; its stated graph scope differs.
The exact four-by-four homotopy result has not been independently audited.

value.rationale: The 2024 primary source explicitly conjectures wedge-of-spheres homotopy for arbitrary rectangular grids and proves only the two-row case. The four-by-four square is the smallest genuinely two-dimensional symmetric square grid beyond that solved two-row regime. Its exact homotopy type spans two distinct dimensions and distinguishes the perfect-matching subcomplex from the previously indexed ordinary matching complex of the same graph. The class of finite exact natural invariants qualifies independently of a general recurrence; the certificate has a complete and re-runnable combinatorial proof, and the nonzero lower homology yields a non-shellability consequence. No general-grid theorem is claimed.
